source.title: Misalignment of Low-Loss Regions Causes Grokking
source.authors: Yong-Ding Tian; Zaid Al-Ars; Maksim Kitsak; P. Hofstee

record.tranche_reason: The study reproduces grokking but also reports anti-grokking counterexamples and argues that grokking depends on alignment between training and validation low-loss regions, refining when the phenomenon should occur.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking and anti-grokking behavior, as well as a Fourier-component diagnostic. It also reports Slingshot spikes in an anti-grokking run; this is recorded as a related finding not covered by the claim versions. General statements about proposed explanations from cited work are not treated as new results.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces the original modular-addition grokking setup. It then shows that a symmetry-preserving split with the same training fraction, smaller training fractions and larger or other modular datasets give no grokking. It also tests whether the Fourier progress signal predicts the absence of grokking. These are its own results arguing that V1 needs restating.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that misalignment of training and validation low-loss regions, set by architecture and data, is the primary cause of grokking. Learning rate, weight decay and initialization are secondary and cannot produce grokking when the regions are well aligned. Grokking is read as a sign of training data that is insufficient relative to model capacity; larger models increase misalignment. The symmetry-preserving split is a counterexample to Slingshot, Fourier-circuit and raw-size-threshold indicators.
record.recipe_differences: Reuses the small transformer modular-arithmetic setup, including the original 97-modulus addition task, but adds symmetry-controlled partitions, altered training fractions, other modular functions, nested datasets, and learning-rate/weight-decay phase sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with train/validation partition structure and same-partition ratio, training fraction, dataset construction and function, and learning-rate/weight-decay settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Slingshot training-loss spikes persist in the anti-grokking run, which never groks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slingshot spikes alone do not reliably indicate that grokking will occur.

record.problems: The alignment account is probed indirectly through phase diagrams rather than direct low-loss-region volume measurements. Several phase results are qualitative, and the paper does not quantify how the delay changes with training-set size. The authors also note that modular arithmetic is noise-free, the symmetry-based knowledge may not transfer to general datasets, and the 50% split is uncommon in practical settings.

untested.parts: How the step delay to the validation jump scales with training-set size; only the presence or absence of a complete transition at selected fractions is reported.
Gradual formation of the Fourier circuit over training, removal of memorizing components, and whether progress measures anticipate the jump in grokking runs.
Non-algorithmic data and initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich switching. MNIST/CIFAR are only cited.
LLM pretraining or fine-tuning; not tested.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size under weight decay, and ungrokking. Weight decay is swept, but low-norm circuit selection is not measured.
Whether runs converge to the same algorithm. Mode connectivity between runs is a loss-path result, not an algorithm comparison.
Controls on optimizer instabilities or softmax floating-point effects; numerical precision is only discussed.

missing.what: Model-size effect on phase diagrams for Dmod(x+y,97). The 4-layer/width-256 model shows Grok cells across most of the grid with rare Comprehension. The 1-layer/width-64 model shows few Grok cells and more Comprehension.
Function dependence at m=97. x^2+y^2 is almost all Comprehension (one Grok cell); x+y and 2x^2+y show many Grok cells.
At m=997, phase diagrams for x+y, xy, x^2+2y^2 and x^2+2y^2+xy show no Grok cells, only Comprehension or Confusion.
Phase diagram for Dmod(x+y,97). The weight-decay-0 column is mostly Memorization, while nonzero weight decay gives Grok cells; this bears on the hyperparameter dependence of V1.
missing.locator: Appendix J Figure 18 / Appendix K Figure 22

missing.what: Intermediate same-partition ratios of 90% and 80% in Figure 12.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The reproduced grokking run uses AdamW with weight decay 0 and dropout 0.1, so grokking occurs without explicit weight decay; this was not used as a V5 test. The alignment account itself is probed only indirectly through phase-cell counts. The training budget is 150k epochs, scaled down linearly for larger datasets, so 'no grokking' cells could partly reflect budget limits.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not quantify how the number of optimization steps to the validation jump changes as training-set size shrinks; it compares whether complete grokking occurs under selected training fractions and splits.

The anti-grokking Fourier diagnostic tests whether a Fourier signal tracks progress in that setting. The paper does not track formation of the circuit over training or measure removal of memorizing components.
No non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale/weight-norm lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The paper sweeps weight decay but does not test whether low norm selects a more efficient generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
The study does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Numerical precision is discussed as part of the model specification, but adaptive-optimizer or softmax numerical-artifact explanations are not controlled experimentally.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.operation_detail: Train on the modular-addition task using the reproduced grokking setup.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy over epochs
rows.value: The paper reports that validation accuracy increases only long after the model has overfit the training partition.
rows.note: The paper says it reproduces grokking in this setup.
rows.check: Correct. The reproduced recipe uses AdamW with weight decay 0.0 and dropout 0.1 (Appendix A); the condition should record this.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.operation_detail: Train with the same hyperparameters as the ordinary setup, using a split that keeps each symmetric pair in one partition.

conditions.value: 100% of paired samples (a,b) and (b,a) assigned to the same partition

rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy and loss over epochs
rows.baseline: Random-partition grokking setup; no numeric baseline stated.
rows.value: Validation accuracy remains low and validation loss does not decrease; the paper states that this split does not produce grokking.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded standard deviation across runs; no numeric value stated.
rows.note: The split is described as the only change relative to the ordinary setup.
rows.check: Correct. Add that the result is over 10 seeds and splits at the same ~50% fraction (4,705/4,704).

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.operation_detail: Vary the proportion of symmetric sample pairs assigned to the same partition.
rows.measure: Whether training and validation accuracy show a complete grokking trajectory
rows.value: No complete grokking trajectory is observed; symmetry-aware training coverage is 0.648.
rows.note: The paper compares this with a clear trajectory at a 60% same-partition ratio.
rows.check: Correct. Figure 12 also shows 90% and 80% ratios, which the rows do not cover separately.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for strict absence versus partial grokking. The text establishes no complete trajectory at 70%, with realized coverage 0.648; it also describes grokking gradually reappearing toward 70%.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, final paragraph; Appendix H.1, Figure 12 and Table 2.
source_check.problem: No complete transition does not establish no effect beyond baseline, as required for absent.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.operation_detail: Vary the proportion of symmetric sample pairs assigned to the same partition.
rows.measure: Whether training and validation accuracy show a complete grokking trajectory
rows.value: A clear grokking trajectory is recovered; symmetry-aware training coverage is 0.680.
rows.note: The paper says grokking gradually recovers as the same-partition ratio decreases.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy over epochs
rows.value: Validation accuracy remains below one and no complete grokking transition is observed; training coverage is 0.637.
rows.note: The paper compares this with a clear delayed rise at 45% training.
rows.check: Correct. Coverage 0.637 is an expected value from a formula (Table 2), not measured on the realized split.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for strict absence versus an incomplete transition. At 40% training, validation accuracy remains below one and no complete transition is observed. Coverage 0.637 is formula-based expected coverage.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix H.1, Figure 13(a), Table 2; Appendix A for the training horizon.
source_check.problem: Failure to complete a transition does not establish absence of delayed validation improvement.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy over epochs
rows.value: Training accuracy reaches one first and validation accuracy rises substantially later, producing a clear grokking trajectory; training coverage is 0.695.
rows.note: This comparison is about presence of a complete delayed transition, not measured optimization delay as a function of training size.
rows.check: Correct. Coverage 0.695 is also a formula-based expectation.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.operation_detail: Measure Fourier components of the neuron-logit map in the anti-grokking run.

conditions.value: 100% of symmetric pairs assigned to the same partition

rows.baseline: Fourier components in the grokking case; no numeric baseline stated.
rows.value: Some frequencies have larger components than others, but concentration is much weaker; the paper says the signal suggests slight progress despite no progress toward grokking.
rows.note: This tests the diagnostic in an anti-grokking setting, not the full temporal formation or removal of circuits.
rows.check: This is a single end-of-training snapshot of Fourier norms in the non-grokking run, not a time series. It bears only on whether the measure is specific to grokking, not on gradual formation before a jump. The baseline is the grokked model's spectrum (Fig. 2b).

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Fourier concentration is weaker in the anti-grokking model, but this comparison does not measure gradual circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, or temporal anticipation of a jump.
source_check.problem: Weak snapshot concentration is not a partial measurement of V2's temporal mechanism.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate and weight decay and classify the resulting learning phase.
rows.value: No Grokking cells are observed across the tested n values; Memorization cells decrease and eventually vanish as n increases, while Comprehension cells appear and become more frequent.
rows.note: This is an indirect alignment probe, not a direct measurement of low-loss-region volume. The authors state that the effective information carried by these training partitions remains below the threshold they posit for grokking.
rows.check: The condition should note a constant LR schedule (not cosine), shared initialization and seed across cells, and a skip-after-two-confusion shortcut (Appendix F). The training fraction is not stated beyond 'random partition'. Targets are mod 1997 and n is the operand-domain size.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 7; Appendices F and N.

rows.subject: Mgrok
rows.operation_detail: Compare phase diagrams across conventional modular datasets with different moduli.
rows.value: Memorization cells decrease and eventually disappear as m increases; Comprehension cells emerge and become more prominent; Grokking cells are mainly observed at intermediate m.
rows.note: The paper cautions that these datasets are not nested, so this is a cross-dataset comparison rather than a monotonic shrinkage test.
rows.check: Correct. The datasets are non-nested and the comparison is qualitative; the training fraction is not stated explicitly in Appendix E.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E, Figure 10; Appendix N states the general 50% training split.

relationships.condition: Original Dmod(x+y,97) random split, 45% random training fraction, and 60% same-partition ratio
relationships.reason: Validation accuracy rises long after training accuracy saturates in these settings (R1, R4, R6).
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy rose long after training accuracy saturated under the original random split, 45% random training fraction, and 60% same-partition ratio.

source_check.condition: Original Dmod(x+y,97) random split, 45% random training fraction, and 60% same-partition ratio
source_check.reason: R1, R4 and R6 report delayed validation improvement or a clear grokking trajectory. They do not separately establish monotonic growth of delay as training size shrinks.

relationships.condition: Symmetry-preserving splits (100% and 70% same-partition ratio) at the same training fraction
relationships.reason: Grokking is absent over 10 seeds when symmetric pairs share a partition, although sample count and recipe are unchanged (R2, R3).
relationships.display_finding: Grokking was absent across 10 seeds when symmetric pairs shared a partition, despite unchanged training size and training procedure.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Symmetry-preserving splits (100% and 70% same-partition ratio) at the same training fraction
source_check.reason: Partition structure limits complete grokking at unchanged sample count. Ten-seed replication applies explicitly to the 100% construction; the 70% result establishes no complete trajectory, rather than strict absence.

relationships.reason: No complete transition within 150k epochs, so below a threshold the delay does not merely grow but the jump is not observed (R5).
relationships.display_finding: No complete transition occurred within 150,000 epochs.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R5 reports no complete transition within the training horizon, whereas R6 reports clear grokking at 45%; this qualifies the shrinking-dataset claim without proving permanent absence.

relationships.condition: Multiplication datasets across operand-domain sizes and moduli, LR/weight-decay sweeps
relationships.reason: No Grokking cells appear in the nested xy sweep; in the non-nested sweep grokking appears mainly at intermediate moduli, giving way to comprehension or confusion (R8, R9).
relationships.display_finding: The nested multiplication sweep showed no grokking, while the non-nested sweep showed it mainly at intermediate moduli, with immediate generalization or failed learning elsewhere.

source_check.condition: Multiplication datasets across operand-domain sizes and moduli, LR/weight-decay sweeps
source_check.reason: Figure 7 reports no Grokking cells; Figure 10 reports Grokking mainly at intermediate moduli. The effect depends on dataset and training conditions.

relationships.reason: A weak Fourier concentration appears without any grokking, so the signal is not specific to an upcoming jump. Only one snapshot is examined (R7).
relationships.display_finding: The final snapshot showed weak Fourier concentration despite no grokking, demonstrating that this signal was not specific to an upcoming transition.

tranche.reason: The controlled partition counterexample and phase comparisons argue that sample count and proposed grokking indicators require qualification.

source_check.notes: R8 uses constant learning rates, shared initialization and seed within each dataset, and inferred Confusion cells after two consecutive Confusion outcomes. Random-split coverages are expectations; symmetry-controlled coverages are computed from realized splits.

statements.correction: Anti-grokking model: some Fourier frequencies have larger components; concentration is much weaker than in the grokked model. No temporal circuit-formation or memorizing-component-removal measurement is reported for this comparison.
statements.problem: The weak Fourier concentration in the anti-grokking model is supported; treating this snapshot as a scope limitation on V2's temporal mechanism is not.
